# Data processing after filtering

```{r}

# ---- Unify variable types ----
# Ordinal/continuous covariates are kept as numeric (sclmeet 1-7, inprdsc 0-6, sclact 1-5,
#   agea, eduyrs, hincfel 1-4, hhmmb, health 1-5); only the nominal variable gndr is converted to factor.

factor_vars <- c("gndr", "cntry")
factor_vars <- intersect(factor_vars, names(dati))
dati[factor_vars] <- lapply(dati[factor_vars], as.factor)

# Response and grouping variables
dati$y     <- factor(dati$fltlnl, ordered = TRUE)   # Target: loneliness (1 = almost never ... 4 = almost always; higher means lonelier)
dati$group <- factor(dati$cntry)                     # Grouping: country (random intercept)

# Covariate set
xnam <- c("sclmeet", "inprdsc", "sclact", "agea", "gndr",
          "eduyrs", "hincfel", "hhmmb", "health")

# Keep only the required columns
vars_keep <- c("y", "group", xnam)
dati_sel  <- dati[, vars_keep]

# Listwise deletion: report how many rows were dropped and which variables the missingness mainly comes from
n_before   <- nrow(dati_sel)
dati_model <- na.omit(dati_sel)
n_after    <- nrow(dati_model)
cat(sprintf("Listwise deletion: %d -> %d rows (%d rows dropped, %.1f%%)\n",
            n_before, n_after, n_before - n_after,
            100 * (n_before - n_after) / n_before))

# Missing counts per variable (to locate the source of missingness)
print(sort(sapply(dati_sel, function(x) sum(is.na(x))), decreasing = TRUE))

str(dati_model)
summary(dati_model)
table(dati_model$y)
table(dati_model$group)
length(levels(dati_model$group))

barplot(table(dati_model$y))
```

# Support functions for prediction and metrics

```{r}

# OMERF prediction: uses the custom method, with random effects included.
predict_omerf_prob <- function(model, y_train, newdata, group_test, lev) {
  mu <- predict.omerf(model, y_train, newdata, group_test, type = "mu")
  mu <- as.data.frame(mu)
  names(mu) <- lev
  response <- predict.omerf(model, y_train, newdata, group_test, type = "response")
  response <- factor(as.character(response), levels = lev, ordered = TRUE)
  list(mu = mu, response = response)
}

# CLMM prediction (with random intercept). Countries unseen in the training set -> random effect set to 0.
predict_clmm_re <- function(model, newdata, xnam, lev) {
  fixed_formula <- as.formula(paste("y ~", paste(xnam, collapse = " + ")))
  X    <- model.matrix(fixed_formula, data = newdata)
  beta <- model$beta
  X    <- X[, names(beta), drop = FALSE]
  eta_fixed <- as.numeric(X %*% beta)

  re_mat <- ranef(model)$group            # Row names = countries, 1 column = intercept
  re_vec <- re_mat[, 1]
  names(re_vec) <- rownames(re_mat)
  b <- re_vec[as.character(newdata$group)]
  b[is.na(b)] <- 0                        # Unseen countries -> 0

  eta   <- eta_fixed + b
  theta <- model$Theta
  K     <- length(lev)

  cumprob <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(newdata), ncol = K - 1)
  for (k in 1:(K - 1)) cumprob[, k] <- plogis(theta[k] - eta)

  prob <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(newdata), ncol = K)
  prob[, 1] <- cumprob[, 1]
  if (K > 2) for (k in 2:(K - 1)) prob[, k] <- cumprob[, k] - cumprob[, k - 1]
  prob[, K] <- 1 - cumprob[, K - 1]

  prob[prob < 0] <- 0
  prob <- prob / rowSums(prob)
  colnames(prob) <- lev

  list(mu = as.data.frame(prob),
       response = factor(lev[apply(prob, 1, which.max)], levels = lev, ordered = TRUE))
}

# ---- Helper to capture warnings uniformly ----
fit_with_warnings <- function(expr) {
  warns <- character(0)
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(
    tryCatch(expr, error = function(e) {
      structure(list(error = conditionMessage(e)), class = "fit_error")
    }),
    warning = function(w) {
      warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  )
  list(fit = fit, warnings = warns)
}

# ---- CLM prediction: unified to list(mu, response) ----
predict_clm_prob <- function(model, newdata, xnam, lev) {
  fixed_formula <- as.formula(paste("y ~", paste(xnam, collapse = " + ")))
  X    <- model.matrix(fixed_formula, data = newdata)
  beta <- model$beta
  X    <- X[, names(beta), drop = FALSE]
  eta  <- as.numeric(X %*% beta)
  theta <- model$Theta
  K    <- length(lev)

  cumprob <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(newdata), ncol = K - 1)
  for (k in 1:(K - 1)) cumprob[, k] <- plogis(theta[k] - eta)

  prob <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(newdata), ncol = K)
  prob[, 1] <- cumprob[, 1]
  if (K > 2) for (k in 2:(K - 1)) prob[, k] <- cumprob[, k] - cumprob[, k - 1]
  prob[, K] <- 1 - cumprob[, K - 1]

  prob[prob < 0] <- 0
  prob <- prob / rowSums(prob)
  colnames(prob) <- lev

  list(mu = as.data.frame(prob),
       response = factor(lev[apply(prob, 1, which.max)], levels = lev, ordered = TRUE))
}

# ---- OrdinalForest prediction: unified to list(mu, response) ----
predict_of_unified <- function(model, newdata, xnam, lev) {
  nd <- newdata[, xnam, drop = FALSE]
  p  <- predict(model, newdata = nd)
  prob <- as.data.frame(p$classprobs)
  # classprobs column names may be "1","2",... or the level characters
  if (!all(as.character(lev) %in% names(prob))) {
    if (ncol(prob) == length(lev)) names(prob) <- as.character(lev)
  }
  prob <- prob[, as.character(lev), drop = FALSE]
  names(prob) <- lev
  resp <- factor(as.character(p$ypred), levels = lev, ordered = TRUE)
  list(mu = prob, response = resp)
}



# Square confusion matrix with all levels.
confusion_full <- function(y_true, y_pred, lev) {
  tab <- table(
    factor(y_true, levels = lev, ordered = TRUE),
    factor(y_pred, levels = lev, ordered = TRUE)
  )
  dimnames(tab) <- list(observed = lev, predicted = lev)
  tab
}

# Fallback for ordinal index, if OrdinalClassificationIndex is not available.
ordinal_index_safe <- function(cm) {
  if (!exists("OrdinalClassificationIndex")) return(NA_real_)
  tryCatch(
    OrdinalClassificationIndex(cm, nrow(cm)),
    error = function(e) { message("OrdinalClassificationIndex failed: ",
                                  conditionMessage(e)); NA_real_ }
  )
}

# Fallback for newindex, if the function is not available.
newindex_safe <- function(mu, y_num, K) {
  if (!exists("newindex")) return(NA_real_)
  if (is.null(mu)) return(NA_real_)          # The majority-class baseline has no probability matrix
  tryCatch(
    newindex(mu, y_num, K)$norm.index,
    error = function(e) { message("newindex failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); NA_real_ }
  )
}

# Cohen's Weighted Kappa for ordinal response.
# weights = "quadratic" penalizes distant errors more heavily;
# use weights = "linear" for linear penalization.
weighted_kappa_safe <- function(y_true, y_pred, lev, weights = "quadratic") {
  y_true <- factor(y_true, levels = lev, ordered = TRUE)
  y_pred <- factor(y_pred, levels = lev, ordered = TRUE)

  tab <- table(y_true, y_pred)
  n <- sum(tab)
  K <- length(lev)

  if (n == 0 || K < 2) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  d <- abs(row(tab) - col(tab))
  if (weights == "linear") {
    W <- d / (K - 1)
  } else if (weights == "quadratic") {
    W <- (d / (K - 1))^2
  } else {
    stop("weights must be 'linear' or 'quadratic'")
  }

  O <- tab / n
  E <- outer(rowSums(tab), colSums(tab)) / n^2

  den <- sum(W * E)
  if (den == 0) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  1 - sum(W * O) / den
}

# Macro-averaged precision (one-vs-rest per class, then averaged)
macro_precision <- function(y_true, y_pred, lev) {
  prec <- sapply(lev, function(c) {
    tp <- sum(y_true == c & y_pred == c)
    fp <- sum(y_true != c & y_pred == c)
    if ((tp + fp) == 0) return(NA) else return(tp / (tp + fp))
  })
  mean(prec, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Macro-averaged recall (one-vs-rest per class, then averaged)
macro_recall <- function(y_true, y_pred, lev) {
  rec <- sapply(lev, function(c) {
    tp <- sum(y_true == c & y_pred == c)
    fn <- sum(y_true == c & y_pred != c)
    if ((tp + fn) == 0) return(NA) else return(tp / (tp + fn))
  })
  mean(rec, na.rm = TRUE)
}

model_metrics <- function(name, pred, y_true, lev) {
  y_num <- as.numeric(y_true)
  pred_num <- as.numeric(pred$response)
  cm <- confusion_full(y_true, pred$response, lev)

  data.frame(
    model = name,
    accuracy = mean(y_num == pred_num),
    recall = macro_recall(y_num, pred_num, seq_along(lev)),
    precision = macro_precision(y_num, pred_num, seq_along(lev)),
    rmse = sqrt(mean((y_num - pred_num)^2)),
    mae = mean(abs(y_num - pred_num)),
    ordinal_classification_index = ordinal_index_safe(cm),
    adjusted_rand_index = adj.rand.index(y_num, pred_num),
    cohen_kappa = cohen.kappa(cbind(y_num, pred_num))$kappa,
    cohen_weighted_kappa = weighted_kappa_safe(
      y_true = y_true,
      y_pred = pred$response,
      lev = lev,
      weights = "quadratic"
    ),
    new_index = newindex_safe(pred$mu, y_num, length(lev))
  )
}
```


# Train/test split — 5-fold cross-validation

```{r}
n_folds <- 5

# ---- Fold assignment: within each country, stratify by y and randomly split into 5 parts, then combine ----
# Ensures: each fold holds about 1/5 of each country (cntry distribution close to the population)
#        plus balanced y within each country (y distribution close to the population),
#        and each observation is tested only once (no duplication).
set.seed(1999)
fold_id <- integer(nrow(dati_model))
for (g in levels(dati_model$group)) {
  idx <- which(dati_model$group == g)
  yg  <- droplevels(dati_model$y[idx])
  fold_g <- integer(length(idx))
  for (cl in levels(yg)) {
    j <- which(yg == cl)
    fold_g[j] <- sample(rep(seq_len(n_folds), length.out = length(j)))
  }
  fold_id[idx] <- fold_g
}
cat("Sample size per fold:\n"); print(table(fold_id))

results_list <- vector("list", n_folds)
pred_list    <- vector("list", n_folds)
ranef_list   <- vector("list", n_folds)
conv_list    <- vector("list", n_folds)
warn_list    <- vector("list", n_folds)

for (fold in seq_len(n_folds)) {
  cat("\n===== Fold", fold, "/", n_folds, "=====\n")
  t_fold <- Sys.time()

  test_idx  <- which(fold_id == fold)
  train_idx <- which(fold_id != fold)
  data_train <- droplevels(dati_model[train_idx, ])
  data_test  <- dati_model[test_idx, ]

  # ---- Align levels: align the test-set factor levels to the training set (unseen levels -> NA) ----
  for (v in names(data_train)) {
    if (is.factor(data_train[[v]])) {
      data_test[[v]] <- factor(data_test[[v]],
                               levels = levels(data_train[[v]]),
                               ordered = is.ordered(data_train[[v]]))
    }
  }

  # ---- Report and filter NAs produced by level alignment (no longer silent) ----
  na_group <- is.na(data_test$group)
  na_cov   <- rowSums(is.na(data_test[, xnam, drop = FALSE])) > 0
  na_y     <- is.na(data_test$y)
  cat(sprintf("  [filter] group NA=%d | cov NA=%d | y NA=%d\n",
              sum(na_group), sum(na_cov & !na_group),
              sum(na_y & !na_group & !na_cov)))
  data_test <- data_test[!(na_group | na_cov | na_y), ]
  if (nrow(data_test) == 0) { cat("  [skip] test set was filtered to empty\n"); next }

  y           <- data_train$y
  group       <- data_train$group
  cov         <- data_train[, xnam]
  lev         <- levels(y)
  y_test_orig <- data_test$y

  # Guard: the training set must have no empty groups
  if (any(table(group) == 0)) { cat("  [skip] training set has empty groups\n"); next }

  tag <- function(m, split) { m$split <- split; m$fold <- fold; m }
  rows_list <- list()

  # =========================================================
  # 1. OMERF
  # =========================================================
  fit <- tryCatch(
    suppressWarnings(
      omerf(y = y, cov = cov, group = group, xnam = xnam,
            znam = NULL, bizero = NULL, itmax = 200, toll = 0.1)
    ),
    error = function(e) { cat("  [omerf error]", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL }
  )

  if (!is.null(fit)) {
    conv_list[[fold]] <- data.frame(
      fold = fold, converged = fit$converged, n_iter = fit$n.iteration
    )
    pred <- tryCatch(
      predict_omerf_prob(fit, y, data_test[, c(xnam, "group")], data_test$group, lev),
      error = function(e) { cat("  [omerf predict error]", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL }
    )
    if (!is.null(pred)) {
      m_omerf_test  <- tag(model_metrics("omerf", pred, y_test_orig, lev), "test")
      pred_tr       <- predict_omerf_prob(fit, y, data_train[, c(xnam, "group")], group, lev)
      m_omerf_train <- tag(model_metrics("omerf", pred_tr, y, lev), "train")
      rows_list[[length(rows_list) + 1]] <- rbind(m_omerf_test, m_omerf_train)
      pred_list[[fold]]  <- pred
      ranef_list[[fold]] <- ranef(fit$clmm.model)$group[, 1]
    }
  }

  # =========================================================
  # 2. CLMM (random-intercept baseline)
  # =========================================================
  clmm_formula <- as.formula(paste("y ~", paste(xnam, collapse = " + "), "+ (1 | group)"))
  clmm_res <- fit_with_warnings(
    clmm(clmm_formula, link = "logit", data = data_train,
         Hess = TRUE,
         control = clmm.control(maxIter = 100, gradTol = 1e-3, maxLineIter = 30))
  )
  clmm_fit   <- clmm_res$fit
  clmm_warns <- length(clmm_res$warnings)

  if (!inherits(clmm_fit, "fit_error")) {
    pc_test  <- tryCatch(predict_clmm_re(clmm_fit, data_test,  xnam, lev), error = function(e) NULL)
    pc_train <- tryCatch(predict_clmm_re(clmm_fit, data_train, xnam, lev), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(pc_test) && !is.null(pc_train)) {
      rows_list[[length(rows_list) + 1]] <- rbind(
        tag(model_metrics("clmm", pc_test,  y_test_orig, lev), "test"),
        tag(model_metrics("clmm", pc_train, y, lev),           "train")
      )
    }
  }

  # =========================================================
  # 3. CLM (no-random-effects baseline)
  # =========================================================
  clm_formula <- as.formula(paste("y ~", paste(xnam, collapse = " + ")))
  clm_res <- fit_with_warnings(
    clm(clm_formula, link = "logit",
        data = data_train[, c("y", xnam)],
        Hess = TRUE)
  )
  clm_fit   <- clm_res$fit
  clm_warns <- length(clm_res$warnings)

  if (!inherits(clm_fit, "fit_error")) {
    pc_test  <- tryCatch(predict_clm_prob(clm_fit, data_test,  xnam, lev), error = function(e) NULL)
    pc_train <- tryCatch(predict_clm_prob(clm_fit, data_train, xnam, lev), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(pc_test) && !is.null(pc_train)) {
      rows_list[[length(rows_list) + 1]] <- rbind(
        tag(model_metrics("clm", pc_test,  y_test_orig, lev), "test"),
        tag(model_metrics("clm", pc_train, y, lev),           "train")
      )
    }
  }

  # =========================================================
  # 4. Ordinal Forest (no-random-effects baseline)
  # =========================================================
  of_res <- fit_with_warnings(
    ordfor(depvar = "y", perffunction = "probability",
           data = data_train[, c("y", xnam)])
  )
  of_fit   <- of_res$fit
  of_warns <- length(of_res$warnings)

  if (!inherits(of_fit, "fit_error")) {
    po_test  <- tryCatch(predict_of_unified(of_fit, data_test,  xnam, lev), error = function(e) NULL)
    po_train <- tryCatch(predict_of_unified(of_fit, data_train, xnam, lev), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(po_test) && !is.null(po_train)) {
      rows_list[[length(rows_list) + 1]] <- rbind(
        tag(model_metrics("ordforest", po_test,  y_test_orig, lev), "test"),
        tag(model_metrics("ordforest", po_train, y, lev),           "train")
      )
    }
  }

  # =========================================================
  # 5. Majority baseline (majority-class baseline)
  # =========================================================
  mode_class <- names(which.max(table(y)))   # Use the training-set mode, not the test set
  maj_test   <- factor(rep(mode_class, nrow(data_test)),  levels = lev, ordered = TRUE)
  maj_train  <- factor(rep(mode_class, nrow(data_train)), levels = lev, ordered = TRUE)
  rows_list[[length(rows_list) + 1]] <- rbind(
    tag(model_metrics("majority", list(response = maj_test,  mu = NULL), y_test_orig, lev), "test"),
    tag(model_metrics("majority", list(response = maj_train, mu = NULL), y,           lev), "train")
  )

  # =========================================================
  # Assemble this round's results
  # =========================================================
  results_list[[fold]] <- do.call(rbind, rows_list)

  warn_list[[fold]] <- data.frame(
    fold       = fold,
    model      = c("clmm", "clm", "ordforest"),
    n_warnings = c(clmm_warns, clm_warns, of_warns)
  )

  # ---- Per-fold predictive performance report ----
  res_fold <- results_list[[fold]]
  acc_test <- res_fold[res_fold$split == "test", c("model", "accuracy")]
  cat(sprintf("  test acc: %s\n",
              paste(sprintf("%s=%.3f", acc_test$model, acc_test$accuracy),
                    collapse = " | ")))
  cat(sprintf("  done in %.1f s | clmm_warn=%d | clm_warn=%d | of_warn=%d\n",
              as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t_fold, units = "secs")),
              clmm_warns, clm_warns, of_warns))
}
```
# converge (50) conclude: model comparison table + convergence + boxplots

```{r}
results_all <- do.call(rbind, results_list)   # up to 10 rows per round: 5 models x test/train

# OMERF convergence information
conv_tab <- do.call(rbind, conv_list)
cat("OMERF convergence rate:", mean(conv_tab$converged, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Mean number of iterations:", mean(conv_tab$n_iter, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

metric_cols <- c("accuracy","precision","recall","rmse","mae",
                 "ordinal_classification_index","adjusted_rand_index",
                 "cohen_kappa","cohen_weighted_kappa","new_index")

summarize_metrics <- function(df, split = "test") {
  sub <- df[df$split == split, ]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(sub$model), function(md) {
    g <- sub[sub$model == md, ]
    data.frame(
      model  = md,
      metric = metric_cols,
      mean   = sapply(metric_cols, function(m) mean(g[[m]],   na.rm = TRUE)),
      sd     = sapply(metric_cols, function(m) sd(g[[m]],     na.rm = TRUE))
    )
  }))
}

summary_test  <- summarize_metrics(results_all, "test")
summary_train <- summarize_metrics(results_all, "train")
summary_test
summary_train

saveRDS(results_all, "results_all.rds")
saveRDS(pred_list,   "pred_list.rds")
saveRDS(ranef_list,  "ranef_list.rds")
saveRDS(conv_tab,    "conv_tab.rds")

# Test-set accuracy compared by model
p_box <- ggplot(results_all[results_all$split == "test", ],
                aes(x = model, y = accuracy)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  ggtitle("Test accuracy across repetitions (by model)")

p_box                 # display
ggsave("test_accuracy_box.pdf", p_box, width = 6, height = 4)

```

# OMERF full-sample fit (produces ICC)

OMERF uses the fixed covariates in the random forest and the random intercept of `group` in the mixed model.

```{r}
# OMERF full-sample model (100% data fit, for interpretation only)
# Note: no test-set metrics are computed here because all data enter the fit;
# any metric on this data is in-sample (optimistic). Generalization is covered by summary_test above.

dati_model <- droplevels(dati_model)

y_full     <- dati_model$y
group_full <- dati_model$group
cov_full   <- dati_model[, xnam]

omerf1 <- omerf(
  y = y_full, cov = cov_full, group = group_full,
  xnam = xnam, znam = NULL, bizero = NULL,
  itmax = 400, toll = 0.1
)

# 1) Convergence status + CLMM sub-model summary
cat("converged:", omerf1$converged, "| iterations:", omerf1$n.iteration, "\n")
summary.omerf(omerf1)

# 2) Random-effect variance (ICC = sigma^2 / (sigma^2 + pi^2/3))
vc_obj <- VarCorr(omerf1$clmm.model)
print(vc_obj)   # read the random-intercept variance sigma^2 from here
# If vc_obj is a list containing a "group" element, ICC can be computed automatically:
sigma2 <- as.numeric(vc_obj$group)
cat("ICC =", round(sigma2 / (sigma2 + pi^2 / 3), 4), "\n")

# 3) Country random intercepts (country effects), sorted + plot
ranef_omerf <- sort(ranef(omerf1$clmm.model)$group[, 1])
print(ranef_omerf)
barplot(ranef_omerf, names.arg = names(ranef_omerf), las = 2,
        main = "Country random intercepts (OMERF)", ylab = "random effect")
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

```


# Full-sample interpretive models
```{r}
# ---- Full-sample interpretive models ----
lev_full  <- levels(dati_model$y)
y_num_full <- as.numeric(dati_model$y)

of_full <- ordfor(depvar = "y", perffunction = "probability",
                  data = dati_model[, c("y", xnam)])

clmm_full <- clmm(as.formula(paste("y ~", paste(xnam, collapse = " + "), "+ (1 | group)")),
                  link = "logit", data = dati_model, Hess = TRUE)

# ---- Expected y: sum(class index x class probability) ----
exp_y <- function(mu) as.numeric(as.matrix(mu) %*% as.numeric(lev_full))

# ---- predict.fun required by iml (function(model, newdata)) ----
pf_of   <- function(object, newdata) exp_y(predict_of_unified(object, newdata, xnam, lev_full)$mu)

sigma2_clmm <- as.numeric(VarCorr(clmm_full)$group)
icc_clmm    <- sigma2_clmm / (sigma2_clmm + pi^2 / 3)
cat(sprintf("CLMM random-intercept variance = %.4f | ICC = %.4f\n", sigma2_clmm, icc_clmm))
```

## Ordinal forest plots
# Interpretation plots (ordinal forest)

```{r}
# Manual partial dependence (single-row prediction, fast)
pdp_numeric <- function(model, var, cov, xnam, lev, n_grid = 15) {
  base <- cov[1, , drop = FALSE]
  for (v in names(base)) {
    if (is.numeric(base[[v]])) base[[v]] <- stats::median(cov[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  vals <- seq(min(cov[[var]], na.rm = TRUE), max(cov[[var]], na.rm = TRUE), length.out = n_grid)
  y <- numeric(n_grid)
  for (i in seq_along(vals)) {
    d <- base
    d[[var]] <- vals[i]
    pr <- predict_of_unified(model, d, xnam, lev)$mu
    y[i] <- sum(as.numeric(as.character(lev)) * as.numeric(pr[1, ]))
  }
  data.frame(x = vals, y_hat = y, variable = var)
}

# iml permutation importance (subsample + 1 repetition, for speed)
set.seed(1999)
sub_idx <- sample(nrow(cov_full), min(1000, nrow(cov_full)))
pred_of <- Predictor$new(of_full, data = cov_full[sub_idx, ],
                         y = y_num_full[sub_idx], predict.fun = pf_of)
imp_of  <- FeatureImp$new(pred_of, loss = "mse", n.repetitions = 1)

# PDP data (all numeric covariates; gndr is excluded automatically)
key_vars <- names(cov_full)[sapply(cov_full, is.numeric)]
pdp_list <- lapply(key_vars, function(v) pdp_numeric(of_full, v, cov_full, xnam, lev_full))
pdp_df   <- do.call(rbind, pdp_list)

# Figure 1: native variable importance
vi <- sort(of_full$varimp, decreasing = TRUE)
vi_df <- data.frame(variable = names(vi), importance = as.numeric(vi))
vi_df$variable <- factor(vi_df$variable, levels = vi_df$variable)
p_imp_native <- ggplot(vi_df, aes(x = variable, y = importance)) +
  geom_col() + coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Importance", title = "Ordinal forest variable importance")
print(p_imp_native)
ggsave("imp_1_of.tiff", p_imp_native, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300, compression = "lzw")

# Figure 2: iml permutation importance
p_imp_iml <- plot(imp_of)
print(p_imp_iml)
ggsave("imp_2_of.tiff", p_imp_iml, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300, compression = "lzw")

# Figure 3: partial dependence plots
p_pdp <- ggplot(pdp_df, aes(x = x, y = y_hat)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_x", ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Covariate value",
       y = "Expected loneliness (higher values indicate more frequent loneliness)")
print(p_pdp)
ggsave("fig_pdp.tiff", p_pdp, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 300, compression = "lzw")
```
